tg.conclusion: Reviewed Telegram v0.89.0 and v0.90.0 with the exact published command contract (Core 0.412.0): bot store fetch renamed to bot messages sync with unchanged options (the old path points to the new one; a saved permissions.bot.store.fetch is refused until renamed), a banned account returns permission_error (exit 5), contact activity filters by scope: and at: queries, and diagnostic run search uses started_at: predicates instead of --since-time. RU/ES changed guides, changelog and technical reference reviewed; shared search pages moved to the at: query. Native roadmap unchanged from v0.88.0. Narrow source-linked errata remain: the roadmap still lists bot button presses, chats start and chats app as future work; the MCP guide omits setup and long-running watch, serve and bot watch from never-offered commands, names chats delete|clear commands that the contract does not have, leaves upgrade out of the authority-gated list, and gives bot messages sync an ask-by-default key it does not have (its permission is bot.messages); the bot guide calls the start option --from, which the contract names --until-id. Chat notes, emoji reaction rankings, remaining max parity and location remain planned.

max.conclusion: Reviewed MAX v0.72.0 to v0.74.0 (0.73.0 and 0.74.0), release commit d94e520708d5fb9a319b98eb1ebaf15984da3794, Core 0.412.0/Base 0.51.0. Native Russian source and EN/ES translations cover bot store fetch renamed to bot messages sync (old name and permission key refused with the replacement), chats requests confirm|reject --all, webhooks --append, framed --jsonl item/end records for lists and watch (watch --json refused), omitted unknown chat membership, started_at: and at:/scope: query terms, and permission-blocked commands that stay discoverable with their availability in the CLI and MCP catalogues. Bulk join requests shipped in 0.73.0 and left the native roadmap; selecting requests by invite link is not available because MAX does not report a request's link. Four portal corrections fixed upstream were retired (permission paths, search runs MCP arguments, groups confirm/reject, upgrade row); new source-attributed corrections fix the usage guide's claim that --all is refused, the retired requests accept name and the max_write availability row, and keep the retired bot store anchors. Attachment archives stay corrected as shipped. Optional store, event actions, video notes/cloud password, chat pin/archive/unread, personal channel comments and standalone installers remain future. No live account checks or extra release performed.

drive.conclusion: Reviewed released Drive 0.29.0 (Core 0.411.0/Base 0.51.0): download/export destinations use --output and --out is refused; note lists take native text: queries; shared contracts and model catalogues come from Core. The owner included merged PR201: mirrors sync/watch --public-url inserts local PNG/JPEG/GIF images through the owner tunnel, so local images move from Next to the current summary. Remote and roadmap guide overrides retired because the released pages contain them; obsolete scenario availability replacements retired, explicit profile replacements kept. Google app review stays in progress; background watch service and front matter stay next; larger annotation copies and mirror deletion stay later. The isolated published package passed 18 offline checks and a fresh production audit with zero findings (cli-testing PR217). No live Google request, real tunnel image fetch or global upgrade was performed.

memo.conclusion: Reviewed Memo 0.94.0–0.97.0 with exact Core 0.414.0/Base 0.51.0. 0.97.0 adds authenticated HTTP MCP (MEMO-23) through Core’s shared transport, access-code OAuth and revocation, with the same three tools and per-call permissions as stdio; Core 0.414.0 supplies a positional and its flag alternative once, fixing note creation. Intervening releases add search people, Drive files in context, schema-derived list queries (protected:true replaces --filter is:protected), linked-chat caps in project evidence, the inherited --topic-name selector and WhatsApp as a store source. EN/RU/ES remote, MCP, security, index, roadmap, people, search, mail, archive, configuration, how-it-works, usage, generated reference and 0.94–0.97 release notes reviewed; the released changelog has no 0.95.0 section (cli-memo source issue, not corrected here). Roadmap: HTTP moved to current; nothing under Next or Later shipped. 660 synthetic runtime tests pass; no owner data, live tunnel or paid API use.

wa.conclusion: Reviewed WhatsApp v0.7.0 and v0.8.0 with the exact published command contract and package: invite previews (chats inspect), linked-device ids (account sessions list), custom Lists read from synced labels (chats folders list|show; folder writes stay refused), received community comments (messages comments; channels have none, sending stays unavailable), canonical shared command names without aliases, query-based search runs and bot templates list, item/end watch JSONL, permission-denied commands discoverable with availability, and mcp.authority / bot.api gating over MCP. RU/ES changed guides, changelog and technical reference reviewed. Native v0.8.0 moved Cloud API bots and verified attachment archives to current capabilities, so the whole-page roadmap correction was retired. Narrow source-linked errata remain: the roadmap and usage guide dropped old-file downloads although the released attachments guide and media.retry-failed still document the limitation, and the MCP terminal-only list was rebuilt from the 0.8.0 contract. Channel files, business labels, the guide command, broader albums, communities and sent-reaction storage remain planned.
